title: Design journey dead-ends when the loop was started without --req: no way to attach an R-id mid-loop
scenario: Driver runs `tp loop init --design "design a plugin system"` (no --req), authors specs/spec.md, and the pm gate passes. The design step then blocks forever on DoR 'Design must be anchored to a requirement R-id'. `loop gate` and `loop approve` accept no --req flag and requirement_id is only settable in loop.init (loop.py:215), so the flagship v2.2 design flow cannot proceed; the only escape is `tp req new` + a fresh `loop init --design --req R-x`, which silently wipes the in-flight loop. The blocker names neither `tp req new` nor `--req`. Reproduced end-to-end in /tmp/qa2-design.
fix: Either let the pm gate attach the WHAT it just validated (auto-record specs/spec.md as a requirement when design_required and no requirement_id, or add `loop gate pass --req R-x`), or make `loop init --design` without --req refuse up front. At minimum extend the blocker text: 'record one with `tp req new "<title>" --acceptance ...` and restart with `loop init --design --req R-xxxx`'.

title: Design approval fingerprints design/ files only — the requirement the design traces to is not pinned
scenario: After human approval, the anchored R-record's acceptance list is edited in the KB (hand-edit of knowledge/requirements/R-*.md; no engine guard exists). design_current_errors() still passes at every later gate because design_evidence_fingerprint() hashes only design/contract.json, design/design.md, and the visual. Plan proceeds; Evaluate then holds the work to the NEW criteria (_criteria_for prefers the requirement's acceptance, loop.py:970-983) while the approved acceptance_map maps the OLD ones — the requirement→design→validation traceability the contract exists to guarantee is silently broken with all gates green.
fix: Include the anchored requirement record's content hash in design_evidence_fingerprint (or re-run the acceptance_map-vs-current-criteria check from design_dod_errors at the plan and em gates, not only at approval).

title: The mandatory solution-design lens evidence is self-attested by the designer the lens judges
scenario: agents/tp-designer.md:20 instructs the designer to 'Record exactly one passing solution-design row with concrete evidence and zero blockers' inside its own contract.json, and the DoD validates only shape (verdict=pass, blockers=0, non-empty evidence string). Unlike evaluator/EM evidence — separate files bound into the submission fingerprint (loop.py:1322-1324) — nothing binds this row to an actual independent lens run, so a designer that skipped or failed the lens can still write a passing row and reach human approval. This contradicts the harness's own separation-of-duties principle ('the grader never grades their own spec') and the lens charter's 'do not pass on prose confidence alone'.
fix: Have the design step's routed solution-design lens (already dispatched by loop next) write its verdict to its own artifact (e.g. .em-review/lens-solution-design/findings.json or design-review/), include that path in the design evidence fingerprint, and make design_dod_errors read the artifact instead of the designer-authored contract field.

title: Designed-edge realization proof is self-referential for edges the scanner cannot see
scenario: A design proposes 'orders/cancellation -> contract:order-cancelled-v2 : provides'. The import scanner can never produce that edge, so the only way it enters the as-built graph is a reviewer hand-running `tp graph edge` (as skills/tp-engineering/SKILL.md:67 instructs). design_review_errors' 'as-built graph is missing designed edges' check (lines 481-489) then passes on the reviewer's own recorded assertion — it proves the edge was typed into graph.json, not that the code actually publishes the event. A design 'realized' this way can be fully non-functional yet pass module/edge/contract conformance.
fix: For recorded (non-scanner) designed edges, require per-edge evidence in meta.design (file:line, test, or probe — mirroring the evaluator's graph dispositions) instead of, or in addition to, mere presence in the as-built edge set.

title: Stale-graph design blocker omits its remedy while the sibling missing-graph blocker names it
scenario: Design DoR in /tmp/qa2-design after a new commit: blocker 'baseline dependency graph is stale for the current HEAD' gives no next action, while line 122's missing-graph variant says 'run graph scan'. A driver seeing only the stale variant must guess the same command applies.
fix: Append '— run `tp graph scan` to refresh it' to the stale-graph blocker.

title: Absent open_questions reported as 'must be a list' instead of naming the required empty-list remedy
scenario: Design gate in /tmp/qa2-design with a contract that simply omits open_questions (a field no schema doc surfaced as mandatory) fails with 'design open_questions must be a list' — reads like a type error, not 'the field is required; write "open_questions": [] when there are none'.
fix: Change the message to 'design open_questions is required — list unresolved questions, or [] when none'.

title: Contract-id prefix rules diverge between Design DoD and plan DoR — an approvable design can be un-plannable
scenario: Design DoD accepts edge nodes (and hence contract ids appearing as nodes) prefixed contract:, resource:, svc:, or ext: (line 258-260) and never validates the contracts[] ids' prefixes at all. Plan DoR accepts only contract:/resource: on task contract ids (depgraph.py:800-804). A design whose contract id is 'svc:billing' passes DoD and gets human approval; design_plan_errors then forces the id verbatim onto plan tasks, where readiness rejects it — the approved design cannot be planned without a new design round.
fix: Enforce the contract:/resource: prefix on contracts[].id in design_dod_errors, matching the downstream readiness rule (the reference doc's example already uses the contract: prefix).

title: 'Alerts or an explicit none rationale' is not modeled — the schema cannot distinguish an alert from a skip rationale
scenario: The error text promises an alternative ('alerts or an explicit none rationale are missing') but the check is just text_list(alerts): `"alerts": ["none"]` passes, and a reviewer of the contract cannot tell an actionable alert from a rationale-for-none. The visualization block got the structured pattern (required:false + reason); observability did not, so this row of the schema is unreviewable as specified.
fix: Mirror the visualization pattern: either a non-empty alerts list or {"none": true, "reason": "…"}, validated distinctly.

title: meta.design.drift is dead-on-pass: no representation exists for explained/accepted drift
scenario: Any non-empty drift list fails the review gate (and verdict must be 'conformant'), so a passing review can never carry a drift record — the field's only legal value on success is []. A reviewer who finds a benign, explained deviation must either fail the whole review or leave the field empty, which incentivizes under-reporting; and the error text 'unexplained design drift' misstates the actual any-drift rule.
fix: Either rename the check and error to the real rule ('any recorded drift blocks; return through Design') everywhere it surfaces, or add a human-approved accepted_drift list distinct from blocking drift.
